claim.pdf_says: BLOCK CONTAINS [integer-1 TO] integer-2 {RECORDS / CHARACTERS} (RECORDS underlined; CHARACTERS printed WITHOUT underline)
claim.why_it_matters: Underlining was added to CHARACTERS in the BLOCK CONTAINS clause of the Relative I-O FD general format. In the printed diagram CHARACTERS is an optional word (not underlined), so 'BLOCK CONTAINS 512' with neither word is legal; the markdown makes CHARACTERS a key word, i.e. one of the two words must be written, which is falsely restrictive.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered page 444 (VIII-14) at 300 dpi and cropped the BLOCK CONTAINS braces: RECORDS carries an underline; CHARACTERS directly below it has no underline at all. The markdown (page-444.md line 24) writes <u>CHARACTERS</u>. Under the 1985 notation an underlined word is a key word required when its option is selected, and braces without choice bars mean exactly one option explicitly specified or implicitly selected; with CHARACTERS not underlined it is optional and is the implicit choice, so 'BLOCK CONTAINS 512' is legal. Marking it underlined turns an optional word into a key word, a genuine normative difference.
